26-sf2-qb-1393.solution: Differentiate: dR/dx = 320 − 8x = 0, so x = 40. The second derivative is −8, which is negative, so this is a maximum, with R(40) = 12,800 − 6,400 = 6,400. Revenue peaks at 40 rentals.
26-sf2-qb-1393.trick: Factor the revenue as 4x(80 − x). The zeros are x = 0 and x = 80, and a parabola peaks halfway between its zeros, so the answer is 40.

26-sf2-qb-1401.solution: After 3 years the amount is A = P(1 + r)ⁿ = 100,000 × 1.1³ = 100,000 × 1.331 = ₦133,100. The interest alone would be ₦33,100, but that is not an option, so the options are asking for the amount. The answer is ₦133,100.
26-sf2-qb-1401.trick: 1.1 cubed is 1.331, so the amount is 133,100. Or eliminate: simple interest would give 100,000 + 3 × 10,000 = 130,000, compounding adds a little more, and only ₦133,100 is above 130,000.
26-sf2-qb-1401.computed: ₦133,100 as the amount (the interest alone is ₦33,100)
26-sf2-qb-1401.comment: The question asks for the compound interest, which is ₦33,100, but the keyed option ₦133,100 is the total amount after 3 years. Since ₦33,100 is not offered, the wording should say amount rather than interest.

26-sf2-qb-1406.trick: Divide by 1,000, which is the length factor 10 cubed. In practice, slide the decimal point three places left: 2,500 becomes 2.5.

26-sf2-qb-1410.solution: A scale of 1:1000 means the real turbine is 1,000 times the model. So the full height is 30 cm × 1,000 = 30,000 cm, which is 300 m.
26-sf2-qb-1410.trick: Add three zeros to 30 to get 30,000 cm. Drop two zeros for metres: 300 m.

26-sf2-qb-1414.solution: 1 dm = 10 cm, so 1 dm³ = 10 × 10 × 10 = 1,000 cm³, and 1,000 cm³ is exactly 1 litre. So 3,000 dm³ = 3,000 L.
26-sf2-qb-1414.trick: One cubic decimetre is one litre, so the number does not change: 3,000.

26-sf2-qb-1446.solution: Take the 30° as the angle between the ladder and the ground. The height reached is the side opposite that angle, so sin 30° = 10 ÷ L. Then L = 10 ÷ 0.5 = 20 m.
26-sf2-qb-1446.trick: In a right triangle with a 30° angle, the side opposite it is half the hypotenuse. So the ladder is double the height: 2 × 10 = 20 m.
26-sf2-qb-1446.computed: 20 m (30° taken from the ground; about 11.5 m if taken from the wall)
26-sf2-qb-1446.comment: The question does not say whether the 30° is measured from the ground or from the wall. From the ground the ladder is 10 ÷ sin 30° = 20 m, the keyed option. From the wall it would be 10 ÷ cos 30° ≈ 11.5 m, which is not offered.

26-sf2-qb-1449.solution: The modulus of a + bi is √(a² + b²). So |3 + 4i| = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5.
26-sf2-qb-1449.trick: 3, 4 and 5 form a well known right triangle, so the modulus is 5 at once.

26-sf2-qb-1452.trick: 6,000 is 20% of 30,000. Spread over 4 years, that is 20 ÷ 4 = 5% a year.

26-sf2-qb-1456.solution: 800 apples sold 4 at a time make 800 ÷ 4 = 200 lots. Revenue = 200 × ₦30 = ₦6,000. Profit = revenue − cost = ₦6,000 − ₦1,600 = ₦4,400.
26-sf2-qb-1456.trick: Count the lots first: 800 ÷ 4 = 200. Then 200 × 30 = 6,000, and taking away 1,600 leaves 4,400.
26-sf2-qb-1456.computed: ₦4,400 as written (none of the three options matches)
26-sf2-qb-1456.comment: As written the profit is ₦4,400, which is not among the options. The option ₦1,200 would fit a cost of ₦4,800 or a price of 4 for ₦14, so a figure in the question was probably recorded wrongly.

26-sf2-qb-1461.solution: The mean (72) is below the median (96), so the skew is negative. Pearson's skewness = 3 × (mean − median) ÷ SD = 3 × (72 − 96) ÷ 12 = 3 × (−24) ÷ 12 = −6.
26-sf2-qb-1461.trick: Mean below median means a negative answer, so 68 is out. Then −24 ÷ 12 = −2, and times 3 gives −6.

26-sf2-qb-1471.trick: 100 − 8 = 92. Also, 108% is impossible, because a probability cannot go above 100%.

26-sf2-qb-1544.solution: Only the first draw matters here. There are 8 + 12 = 20 in the bag, so P(first is red) = 8/20 = 2/5 = 40%.
26-sf2-qb-1544.trick: Ignore the second draw. Each of the 20 is worth 5%, and 8 × 5% = 40%.

26-sf2-qb-1550.solution: Power = work ÷ time = 100 J ÷ 5 s = 20 J/s = 20 W.
26-sf2-qb-1550.trick: Just divide: 100 ÷ 5 = 20. Power is joules per second, so the unit is watts, not percent.

26-sf2-qb-1602.trick: The gap is 160 − 80 = 80. Divide by 4 to get 20, then multiply by 3 to get 60.

26-sf2-qb-1627.trick: 6% for 5 years is 30% of the principal. If 30% is 18,000, then 10% is 6,000, so 100% is 60,000.

26-sf2-qb-1639.solution: CV = (SD ÷ mean) × 100%, so SD = CV × mean = 0.25 × 50 = 12.5 mm.
26-sf2-qb-1639.trick: 25% is a quarter, and a quarter of 50 is 12.5.

26-sf2-qb-1684.trick: Add in thousands: 50 + 25 + 15 = 90. Then 90 ÷ 3 = 30, which is ₦30,000.

26-sf2-qb-1706.trick: The score is 12 above the mean and one SD is 6, so it is exactly 2 SDs up.

26-sf2-qb-1729.solution: Cumulative frequency adds the counts up to a class. A is the top grade, so B or lower means B and C: 15 + 5 = 20 students.
26-sf2-qb-1729.trick: B or lower includes C as well as B, so the answer must be above 15. Only 20 fits.

26-sf2-qb-1759.solution: P(no breakdown in a day) = 1 − 0.75 = 0.25. Taking the days as independent, P(2 days in a row) = 0.25 × 0.25 = 0.0625 = 6.25%.
26-sf2-qb-1759.trick: 0.25 is 1/4, so two days is 1/4 × 1/4 = 1/16, which is 6.25%.

26-sf2-qb-1774.solution: Correlation r = cov ÷ (σx × σy), so σx = cov ÷ (r × σy) = 50 ÷ (0.625 × 8) = 50 ÷ 5 = 10.

26-sf2-qb-1866.solution: There are 6 + 4 + 2 = 12 marbles. Drawing two without replacement, P(both blue) = 2/12 × 1/11 = 2/132 = 1/66.
26-sf2-qb-1866.trick: Two blue marbles can only come out as one pair among 12 × 11 ÷ 2 = 66 pairs, so 1/66. Also, 1/6 and 1/11 are single steps, so the full answer must be smaller than each.

26-sf2-qb-1916.solution: With 4 values, the median is the mean of the middle two. So the median = (70 + 80) ÷ 2 = 75.
26-sf2-qb-1916.trick: The values are evenly spaced, so the median sits halfway between 70 and 80, which is 75.
